Existing stand & transition

▸Stand · elbow · jackassumed from the old unitTap to edit

Tape the metal that's staying. Each box has a letter — find the same letter on the picture to see exactly what to measure. Leave blank what you can't reach.

StandRoof pitch only — the rest is assumed
The stand is assumed to suit the old unit (4 / 12 roof unless you say otherwise). Open Stand measurements below only if you taped it.
Pitch:—
Stand measurements — assumed, open to dial them in
Elbow / transition at the unit faceStand at the unit and look into the opening
The transition is lined up with the stand and the unit automatically — nudge it on the 3D if it needs moving.

Left opening

Right opening

Jack (roof penetration)Assumed 1" bigger than the elbow face
The jack box is assumed 1" larger than the elbow face (A + 1 wide · B + 1 deep and tall). The two holes inside it are what matters — those are asked below.
Jack measurements — assumed, open to dial them in
Typical jacks:width × depth — the two penetrations sit inside, either side of the divider
The two holes inside the jackThe airflow runs through these

Tape the two holes the air goes through — a hole smaller than its duct is a chokepoint.

Airflow design
The temperatures feed the Manual J (the cooling pair rescales the wall and attic temperature differences, as the app does). Design CFM = size × CFM per ton; a blower that cannot reach it sets the new maximum.

Units we offer kept on this iPad · a texted design carries it

Manual D design point ACCA Manual D — the equipment first, then the ducts on top; the design static starts at the aim and steps 0.05″ only as far as the air needs

Airflow caps max CFM through a spot — the Goettl method

Sizing & rooms

Fit thresholds

Red is always "new is bigger than the space (or the opening)". With no measurements the options are judged against the old equipment. Package units: Stand is green on the deck, orange overhanging up to the limit, red beyond; Metal uses the alignment thresholds for position and opening size.
